# mcp-statement-of-account

<!-- mirror-seo:start -->

**MCP server for customer statements of account, accounts receivable and invoice aging.** The one document that answers what a client actually owes you, aged as at any date, with the chaser drafted.

Works with Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor and any Model Context Protocol client. Runs on your own machine, or hosted with no install.

Product page: <https://mcp.zovo.one/s/statement-of-account> — what it does, the tools it exposes, and a live token endpoint.

## Install

**Hosted, nothing to install.** Get a token from <https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/connect> (the connect page) or <https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/token> (the same token as JSON); a free anonymous one is issued on the spot and a Pro key works the same way. Then point an MCP client at `https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/statement-of-account` over streamable-http and send the token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

If your client cannot set headers, put the token in the path instead: `https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/statement-of-account/t/<token>`. Both forms work. The bare URL with no token answers 401 on `tools/call`, so the token is not optional.

**Claude Desktop, one click.** Download `statement-of-account.mcpb` from the [latest release](https://github.com/theluckystrike/mcp-servers/releases/latest) and double-click it.

**From source.** The mirror is self-contained: every `@theluckystrike/*` dependency is vendored, so a fresh clone builds with no extra setup.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/theluckystrike/mcp-statement-of-account.git
cd mcp-statement-of-account
npm install && npm run build
```

Then point your client at the built entry point:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "statement-of-account": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/absolute/path/to/mcp-statement-of-account/dist/index.js"]
    }
  }
}
```

> `@theluckystrike/mcp-statement-of-account` is **not published on npm yet**, so an `npx -y @theluckystrike/mcp-statement-of-account` command will fail. The three paths above are the working ones and each is exercised by CI.

# forbiz-mcp

**MCP server for [Forbiz](https://forbiz.io), the CRM for AI agents.** Your business continues when your AI changes.

Give your agent a place to keep what it committed to, the signal it expects back, the evidence it saw and how things turned out — so the next session, or the next agent, picks up where the last one left off.

- **No account to start.** The agent opens a provisional workspace by itself with `forbiz_start`. The owner claims it later with a link.
- **Commitments that can be resumed.** Every commitment carries a `commitmentKey`. Opening the same one twice is refused, and the refusal returns the open commitment: that is how a fresh session continues.
- **Evidence is not truth.** What the agent writes is append-only history. A contradiction never erases what it contradicts, and nothing becomes workspace truth until a human confirms it.
- **Who did what is recorded.** Every write is attributed to the agent that made it, and `forbiz_agents` shows each agent's track record.

## Install

Requires Node 18 or later.

**Claude Code**

```bash
claude mcp add forbiz -- npx -y github:tbernabo/forbiz-mcp
```

**Claude Desktop** (`claude_desktop_config.json`) or **Cursor** (`.cursor/mcp.json`)

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "forbiz": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "github:tbernabo/forbiz-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

That is enough: the agent calls `forbiz_start` the first time and the credential is stored in `~/.forbiz-mcp/credential.json`.

**Already have a Forbiz credential?** Add it to the server's environment instead:

```json
"env": { "FORBIZ_API_KEY": "<your credential>" }
```

Credentials starting with `fbzr_` are exchanged automatically for a short-lived token.

# MaxMindDB MCP Server

[![License: ISC](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-ISC-blue.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/ISC)

Look up IP locations and network ownership in GeoIP2, GeoLite2, and custom MMDB databases from your AI assistant.
Search networks, compare databases, and download new databases through MCP.

This is an unofficial project and is not endorsed by MaxMind Inc. For official products and support, visit [maxmind.com](https://www.maxmind.com/).

Try asking:

- "Using MaxMindDB, identify the country and autonomous system for 8.8.8.8."
- "Find the networks belonging to AS13335 within 1.0.0.0/8 in my ASN database."
- "Which databases are available, and when were they built?"

Answers come from your databases. IP geolocation is an estimate, not a device's precise location.
ASN data describes network ownership, not the identity of a person using an address.

## What you need

Provide either existing `.mmdb` files or a [MaxMind account ID and license key](https://www.maxmind.com/en/accounts/current/license-key) with access to the editions you want.
Databases and credentials are not bundled.

The server runs on your computer and requires a client that supports local MCP servers.

## Installation

### Claude Desktop

# tv-vibehack

**Your TV, minus the ads.** Debloat any Android TV / Google TV over ADB and give it a clean,
tvOS-inspired launcher. Hand the prompt to Claude Code or any coding assistant, answer a few
questions about which apps you use, and it does the rest on the real TV.

| Stock home screen | After |
|---|---|
| ![Stock Google TV home with a sponsored ad](docs/stock-home.jpg) | ![tvOS-style launcher](docs/new-home.jpg) |

Everything is reversible: packages are disabled, never uninstalled, and a restore script puts the
stock launcher back.

## Quick start

1. On the TV: Settings → Device Preferences → About → press OK on **Build** seven times → back →
   Developer options → turn on **USB debugging** (and Network/ADB debugging if your TV shows it).
   Keep the TV on and on the same Wi-Fi as your computer.
2. Open Claude Code (or your assistant of choice) on your computer and paste the prompt from
   [`PROMPT.md`](PROMPT.md), filling in your TV model.
3. Accept the "Allow USB debugging?" prompt on the TV when told to, then answer the checklist
   questions (which apps you use, which four go in the dock).

That's it. The assistant backs up, debloats, builds and installs the launcher, and verifies each
step with screenshots from the TV. If you'd rather do it by hand, the pieces are below.

## What's in the repo

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`PROMPT.md`](PROMPT.md) | The prompt. Brand-neutral; the assistant discovers your TV's bloat. |
| [`launcher/`](launcher/) | The tvOS-style launcher. Edit `app/src/main/res/values/config.xml` for your dock, hidden apps and Live TV package, then run `build-and-install.sh`. |
| [`tools/tv.py`](tools/tv.py) | Pure-Python ADB client (shell, batch, push, pull). Works where the stock `adb` is blocked. |
| [`tools/b64push.py`](tools/b64push.py) | Uploads larger files (APKs) as base64 chunks with an md5 check. |
| [`tools/disable.sh`](tools/disable.sh), [`tools/restore.sh`](tools/restore.sh) | Apply or undo a debloat list. |
| [`examples/`](examples/) | Per-TV debloat lists. Add yours, see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). |

## The launcher

A small native Android TV home screen (`com.gathin.tvhome`), built for sets with 1 GB of RAM:

- Pitch-black background, like Apple TV 4K.
- A dock at the bottom in a lighter rounded band with the four apps you choose. The shelf above
  shows the focused dock app's name in large type with an ambient glow sampled from its banner.
  Press Down and the dock slides up to reveal the rest
